In [[mathematics]], the '''Carlitz–Wan conjecture''' classifies the possible [[degree of a polynomial|degrees]] of exceptional polynomials over a [[finite field]] ''F''<sub>''q''</sub> of ''q'' elements. A [[polynomial]] ''f''(''x'') in ''F''<sub>''q''</sub>[''x''] of degree ''d'' is called exceptional over ''F''<sub>''q''</sub> if every [[irreducible polynomial|irreducible]] factor (differing from ''x''&nbsp;−&nbsp;''y'') or (''f''(''x'')&nbsp;−&nbsp;''f''(''y''))/(''x''&nbsp;−&nbsp;''y'')) over ''F''<sub>''q''</sub> becomes reducible over the [[algebraic closure]] of ''F''<sub>''q''</sub>. If ''q''&nbsp;>&nbsp;''d''<sup>4</sup>, then ''f''(''x'') is exceptional [[if and only if]] ''f''(''x'') is a [[permutation polynomial]] over ''F''<sub>''q''</sub>.

The Carlitz–Wan conjecture states that there are no exceptional polynomials of degree ''d'' over ''F''<sub>''q''</sub> if gcd(''d'',&nbsp;''q''&nbsp;−&nbsp;1)&nbsp;>&nbsp;1.

In the special case that ''q'' is [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] and ''d'' is [[parity (mathematics)|even]], this [[conjecture]] was proposed by [[Leonard Carlitz]] (1966) and [[mathematical proof|proved]] by Fried, Guralnick, and Saxl (1993).<ref>{{citation|last1=Fried|first1=Michael D.|author1-link=Michael D. Fried|last2=Guralnick|first2=Robert|author2-link=Robert Guralnick|last3=Saxl|first3=Jan|s2cid=18446871|author3-link=Jan Saxl|doi=10.1007/BF02808112|doi-access=free|issue=1–3|journal=[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]|mr=1239049|pages=157–225|title=Schur covers and Carlitz's conjecture|volume=82|year=1993}}</ref> The general form of the Carlitz–Wan conjecture was proposed by [[Daqing Wan]] (1993)<ref>{{citation|last=Wan|first=Daqing|authorlink=Daqing Wan|editor1-last=Mullen|editor1-first=Gary L.|editor2-last=Shiue|editor2-first=Peter Jau-Shyong|contribution=A generalization of the Carlitz conjecture|isbn=0-8247-8805-2|mr=1199817|pages=431–432|publisher=Marcel Dekker, Inc., New York|series=Lecture Notes in Pure and Applied Mathematics|title=Finite fields, Coding Theory, and Advances in Communications and Computing: Proceedings of the International Conference held at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, Nevada, August 7–10, 1991|volume=141|year=1993}}</ref> and later proved by [[Hendrik Lenstra]] (1995).<ref>{{citation|last1=Cohen|first1=Stephen D.|last2=Fried|first2=Michael D.|author2-link=Michael D. Fried|doi=10.1006/ffta.1995.1027|issue=3|journal=Finite Fields and Their Applications|mr=1341953|pages=372–375|title=Lenstra's proof of the Carlitz–Wan conjecture on exceptional polynomials: an elementary version|volume=1|year=1995|doi-access=free}}</ref>
